title: Effects and safety of periconceptional oral folate supplementation for preventing birth defects
quick: Folic acid before and early in pregnancy helps prevent serious brain and spine birth defects.
details: RR .31 (.17–.58), high certainty.
funding: Review and primary disclosures not fully extracted
limitations: Includes older high-risk and general-population studies; no proof other folate forms equivalent for NTD prevention

title: Prevention of neural tube defects: results of the Medical Research Council Vitamin Study
quick: Folic acid reduced repeat neural tube defects in this high-risk group.
details: 6 vs 21 affected pregnancies; RR .28 (.12–.71).
funding: MRC research group; complete primary support/donations unknown
limitations: Recurrence population; historical high dose not general prophylaxis; overlaps P5-01

title: USPSTF folic acid recommendation; CDC clinician guidance
scope: Average-risk people planning or capable of pregnancy
quick: Folic acid is an established preventive measure; start before conception.
details: 400–800 mcg/day supplement USPSTF; CDC 400 mcg/day at least one month before conception through first three months.
limitations: Higher-risk dosing clinician-directed; not interchangeable with total folate DFE

title: MTHFR Gene Variant and Folic Acid Facts
quick: Common MTHFR variants are not a reason to avoid folic acid.
details: CDC July 16 2026: folic acid intake more important than genotype for blood folate; folic acid has direct prevention evidence.
limitations: Do not claim all folate forms unsafe or identical; rare disorders separate.

title: Calcium supplementation during pregnancy for preventing hypertensive disorders and related problems
quick: Recent evidence questions extra calcium for preventing preeclampsia.
details: RR .83 (.67–1.04), low certainty; >=500-person trials RR .92 (.79–1.05), high certainty; RD 9 fewer per 1000 (17 fewer to 2 more).
financial_ties: Review-level full COI pending; trial-level separate
access: Cochrane HTML funding and indexed abstract
limitations: Trustworthiness exclusions disputed; not dietary requirement; do not change prescribed calcium.

title: Trial trustworthiness assessment: commentary on the Cochrane 2025 systematic review on calcium supplementation during pregnancy
quick: Some researchers disagree about which calcium studies should be included.
details: Authors cite ethics statement in excluded trial and contest reasons; no new independent trial.
financial_ties: Atallah and Torloni coauthored earlier Cochrane versions; Cormick no competing interests declared
access: Publisher HTML funding, competing interests, selected text
limitations: Academic intellectual conflict matters even without commercial funding; excluded trials need independent appraisal.

title: Calcium supplementation for prevention of pre-eclampsia: a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of randomised trials
quick: Overall benefit unclear; starting earlier might matter but needs more research.
details: PE OR .89 (.73–1.07); early PE OR .90 (.25–3.27); modeled estimate at 10 weeks OR .65 (.48–.90), significant nonlinear timing interaction.
funding: UKRI MRC, UN/WHO/World Bank HRP programme, NIHR (institution record describes as US; country label needs verification)
access: University of Birmingham publication abstract and funding; publisher 403
limitations: Correct DR003 overbroad no effect modification statement: gestational start timing interaction reported. Not independent of Cochrane cohorts; not early-start advice.

title: Calcium supplementation commenced before pregnancy for preventing hypertensive disorders and related problems
quick: Starting calcium before pregnancy has not been proven to prevent complications.
details: Evidence from one trial; preterm birth RR .90 (.74–1.10).
limitations: No 3-year prevention recommendation.

title: Two Randomized Trials of Low-Dose Calcium Supplementation in Pregnancy
scope: India and Tanzania 11000 each; 500 vs 1500 mg/day
quick: A lower calcium dose performed similarly for preeclampsia in these settings; neither group received placebo.
details: Preeclampsia noninferiority in both; preterm India 11.4 vs12.8% RR .89 (.80–.98), Tanzania 10.4 vs9.7% RR 1.07 (.95–1.21), latter not noninferior.
limitations: Dose comparison not efficacy vs no calcium; do not generalize setting or self-prescribe.

title: WHO pre-eclampsia fact sheet and calcium recommendation lineage
quick: Calcium is needed for healthy bones; prevention advice depends on diet and clinical circumstances.
details: October 2026 fact sheet still references 2018 calcium guidance; NIH ODS summarizes 1.5–2 g/day in low-intake populations. No superseding final recommendation confirmed.
limitations: Do not use new review to discontinue prescribed prevention; verify guideline release.

title: Probiotics to prevent gestational diabetes mellitus
quick: Probiotic supplements have not proven they prevent gestational diabetes, and a safety concern was found.
details: PE RR 1.85 (1.04–3.29), review high certainty; hypertensive disorders RR 1.39 (.96–2.01).
financial_ties: Authors include investigators in underlying trials; formal disclosure pending
limitations: Specific prevention populations; not fermented food or all strains; no pooling with broader review.

title: The effects of probiotics administration during pregnancy on preeclampsia and associated maternal, fetal, and newborn outcomes
quick: A larger review found no clear benefit or harm for preeclampsia.
details: PE RR 1.14 (.84–1.53), preterm RR .93 (.66–1.30), low certainty.
funding: Gates Foundation INV-038938 and Harry Secomb Foundation IPAP2022/0475
financial_ties: Full COI pending; underlying trials separate
access: Indexed primary abstract and publisher funding
limitations: Broader populations/eligibility; cannot dismiss earlier safety signal; overlapping trials.

title: Probiotics for the Prevention of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus in Overweight and Obese Women: Findings From the SPRING Double-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial
quick: The probiotic trial did not show prevention of gestational diabetes, and more women developed preeclampsia in the probiotic group.
details: PE 9.2% vs 4.9%, p=.09; not definitive alone.
funding: NHMRC and Royal Brisbane and Women's Hospital Foundation reported in prior same-cohort disclosures; Chr Hansen donated active/placebo per prior H002/H003 audit
financial_ties: Product supply linked through secondary reports; primary disclosures not newly verified
access: Primary indexed abstract; inherited funding crosswalk
limitations: Adverse directional result despite in-kind support; full primary funding, exact arms and registry pending.

title: A Randomized Trial of Prenatal n-3 Fatty Acid Supplementation and Preterm Delivery
quick: Extra omega-3 did not clearly reduce early preterm birth overall in this large trial.
details: 61/2734 vs55/2752; adjusted RR 1.13 (.79–1.63); very large for gestational age RR 1.30 (1.02–1.65).
funding: Australian NHMRC, Thyne Reid Foundation; Croda UK and Efamol/Wassen UK donated capsules, no other role reported
financial_ties: Full author disclosure pending; commercial in-kind verified
access: Primary PubMed HTML, NEJM indexed funding
limitations: Different baseline status and comparator from ADORE; not proof fish unnecessary.

title: Higher dose docosahexaenoic acid supplementation during pregnancy and early preterm birth
quick: Higher DHA looked more promising in participants with low DHA levels.
details: 9/540 vs12/492; posterior probability .81; low baseline 5/249 vs9/219, PP .93.
funding: NICHD R01HD083292; DSM donated all capsules
financial_ties: Susan Carlson reported DSM in-kind and outside-work DSM/Mead Johnson fees in institution record
access: Indexed original abstract and university disclosure
limitations: Posterior probability is not individual benefit; no unsupervised high-dose advice.

title: Genotype-informed docosahexaenoic acid dosing based on the FADS Indel to reduce preterm and prolonged gestation
quick: Genetic findings are interesting but not ready for personalized supplement advice.
details: I-allele EPB RR .25 (95% CrI .03–.87); 2/205 vs9/214. D/D EPB 5/191 vs1/151; possible unfavorable subgroup signal.
funding: NIH R01HD083292; no sponsor role; parent trial DSM in-kind
financial_ties: Current paper disclosure must be read with parent trial financial ties; no assumption of new independent cohort
access: Original PLOS HTML and indexed abstract
limitations: Post hoc, small event counts; no genotype/race dosing or tests; preserve GE-H04.

title: Vitamin D supplementation for women during pregnancy
quick: Vitamin D is essential, but extra supplements have not clearly prevented several pregnancy complications.
details: PE RR .53 (.21–1.33), 1 study 165; preterm RR .76 (.25–2.33), 3 studies 1368. 20 prior studies awaiting classification, one excluded for trustworthiness.
limitations: Very uncertain outcomes; not evidence to ignore deficiency.

title: Regimens of vitamin D supplementation for women during pregnancy
scope: Higher vs lower doses; no zero dose arms
quick: Higher doses have not consistently demonstrated extra benefits; two displayed summaries conflict.
details: Cochrane page shows GDM RR .54 (.34–.86), 5 trials 1846; PubMed indexed abstract .85 (.52–1.40), 6 studies 2373. Different sample counts and multiple results; hold both sets.
financial_ties: Full COI and primary trial funding pending
access: Cochrane HTML results vs PubMed indexed abstract, direct PubMed captcha
limitations: Version discrepancy, not evidence of fraud; check DOI version, full tables and correction before chart; no dosage change.

title: Daily oral iron supplementation during pregnancy
quick: Iron supplementation can reduce iron-deficiency anemia.
details: Term iron-deficiency anemia 5.0% vs18.4%; RR .41 (.26–.63), 7 trials 2704 moderate certainty. Maternal anemia RR .30 (.20–.47), 14 trials 13543 low certainty.
access: Indexed primary review abstract; PMC direct captcha
limitations: Reported proportions and pooled RR differ; not individual dose, screening or infant dosing.

title: Daily versus Alternate-Day Iron Supplementation for Pregnant Women with Iron Deficiency Anemia
quick: Taking iron every other day did not clearly work better than daily treatment in this trial.
details: Adjusted Hb difference alternate minus daily -.3 g/dL (-.7 to .1), six weeks; side effects similar.
limitations: Treatment population, not prevention; no self-change in prescribed regimen.

title: Effect of iodine supplementation in pregnant women on child neurodevelopment
scope: 832 women, mild deficiency context; 313 children IQ analysis
quick: Iodine is essential for brain development, but extra iodine did not improve IQ in this trial.
details: Verbal IQ MD -.7 (-2.9–1.5); performance IQ -1.6 (-4.5–1.3).
funding: Swiss National Science Foundation, Nestlé Foundation, Wageningen University and Research, ETH Zurich
financial_ties: Foundation originates from Nestlé donation, states independent governance; current company influence not demonstrated; individual COI pending
limitations: Attrition, timing and baseline status; no inference for severe deficiency or adequate intake guidance.

title: About the Nestlé Foundation
quick: A foundation name does not tell us who controlled a study.
details: Established by Nestlé donation in 1966; foundation describes independent governance.
financial_ties: No verified current company control; independent governance audit pending
limitations: Not a clinical trial or independent verification of governance.

title: Open label, dose escalation trial of creatine monohydrate in pregnancy
quick: Creatine is being studied, but there is not enough evidence to recommend taking it for fetal protection.
details: Dose/tolerability and pharmacokinetics, not proven clinical efficacy.
limitations: No randomized efficacy or long-term safety; preserve research-only status.

title: Prenatal Supplements: Amounts of Some Key Nutrients Differed from Product Labels
quick: Independent tests sometimes find different amounts than the label says.
details: 11/12 at least one deviation; 9/12 vitamin A; vitamin E 28–332% of label; 1 folic acid result potentially concerning; trace lead/cadmium 6/12 below levels likely concerning by FDA metrics.
funding: US GAO commissioned blinded accredited laboratory
limitations: Selected anonymized sample, cannot identify brands or generalize prevalence; no inference all deviations dangerous.

title: Testing Results for Selected Prenatal Supplements
quick: The original testing charts show how measured values compare with labels.
details: Supplemental charts and raw data CSV available.
limitations: PDF and CSV not downloaded or inspected; not another sample.

title: Selecting a dietary supplement with appropriate dosing for 6 key nutrients in pregnancy
quick: Many prenatal labels do not cover every modeled nutrient gap.
details: 69 products including 33 prenatal listed all six; 7 products including 2 prenatal met modeled targets for five nutrients.
limitations: Model assumptions not personalized dose or verified actual product contents; no current brand ranking.

title: Content of selected nutrients and heavy metals in prenatal multivitamins and minerals
quick: Some prenatal vitamins contained less iodine than listed.
details: 20/25 had >20% less iodine than label; 4/25 within 20%, 1/25 >20% higher.
financial_ties: Full COI unknown; direct PMC captcha
limitations: Sampling and assays; no brand recommendation or prevalence estimate.

title: Dietary Supplements and Life Stages: Pregnancy
quick: Food and prenatal supplements can work together to meet nutrient needs.
details: Tables 1 and 2 contain reference intakes and upper limits, with form-specific caveats.
limitations: Not supplement doses; ND is not unlimited safety; use age and stage.

title: Advice about Eating Fish
quick: Fish provides useful nutrients; choose lower-mercury types.
details: 8–12 oz/wk lower-mercury seafood for pregnant/breastfeeding adults; age-specific child guidance separate.
limitations: No fish oil equivalence; allergy/food safety; check current chart.

title: Folate and Folic Acid on the Nutrition and Supplement Facts Labels
quick: Folate on a label and folic acid are measured differently.
details: Look for folic acid mcg in parentheses, not only total mcg DFE.
limitations: Do not convert UL DFE as if same unit.

title: Dietary Supplement Label Database
quick: A label database shows what companies claim, not what a lab tested.
details: Use dated exact labels, manufacturer and serving size.
limitations: Not proof of efficacy, actual contents or current recall status.
